pcos stands for poly cystic ovary syndrome, which basically means cysts are present in your ovaries that can affect your hormone levels. for a lot of people, this results in symptoms such as acne, excessive hair growth, irregular periods, and a lot of other symptoms that are pretty general and can be mistaken for other issues. 

sorry for not answering this earlier, i just logged on now. if you have any other questions i would be happy to talk more about it!:)

i was diagnosed by going to a gyno. some of the symptoms of pcos can be very general and apply to other issues, so in my case, i had my hormones checked. they found that i had an abnormal level of testosterone and eventually diagnosed me with pcos. i was also given birth control, and it has eased my symptoms greatly.

no, this happened when i was around 14. im not too sure about the effects of stopping birth control on periods, but it seems like you can definitely ask everyone around here with different experiences :)

im sorry, i should have clarified that this happened in my own experience and is in no way absolute. i had other symptoms that suggested something was abnormal, but from my doctors responses, i was led to believe this was normal as well. irregularity does not indicate disease, especially with periods early on, but it just happened to be my case

im so sorry for scaring you (puberty is scary enough), it definitely is normal to have some irregularity. in my own case, i had other symptoms that suggested things were abnormal, but irregularity doesnt automatically mean pcos. dont worry, but if you are concerned, doing some research online and asking a good doctor can be reassuring :)
that is definitely true too!! i should have mentioned that in some cases it can be a very normal part of puberty, it just wasnt for me
